The contextual analysis backend

Built around
Anthropic Claude.

Is this action related to the task? Did an untrusted instruction redirect the agent? Claude adds contextual reasoning to the local policy engine—so you can review the evidence, not just a warning.

Read about Claude analysis
01

Two planned connections.

Direct Anthropic BYOK uses your own key. MVP3 adds a TraceRook-operated Claude backend with a company-owned key.

02

An analyst with bounded authority.

Claude can recommend human review. It cannot grant permissions, execute commands, or overrule a deterministic critical denial.

03

Useful offline, too.

The MVP2 design keeps deterministic local rules available when AI analysis is offline, over budget, or disabled.

The native app now connects to the local mock API; synthetic responses make no Claude calls. A separate developer probe validated Anthropic Haiku 5.5. The production Cloud API is deployed; genuine hosted receipts and final native Cloud evidence remain pending. Follow the API integration work.

Privacy is part of the architecture

A smaller data footprint.
A clearer boundary.

The planned analysis pipeline minimizes context on your Mac, redacts it, and checks it again before transmission. Additional code excerpts default off. Redaction can miss secrets; consent and clear limits still matter.

On your Mac

Cloud Demo

The native UI and Cloud Demo are ready to explore. Local development passes 64 Swift tests, 103 backend tests and 22 native appearance checks.
